title: AI literacy
reasoning: Providers and deployers must take measures that support AI literacy of staff who operate or oversee the system; the Omnibus softened the wording from ensuring a sufficient level. Applies since 2 Feb 2025.

title: Prohibited practices
reasoning: None of the prohibited practices are intended. The relevant risk is manipulation or exploiting vulnerability in a customer conversation (Art 5(1)(a)-(b)) and emotion inference. Guardrails G-16 and G-14 keep the system outside them. Re-check when features change.

title: Classification rules
reasoning: The classification reasoning is in 02-eu-ai-act-classification.md. Not Annex III high-risk because the scope excludes creditworthiness and insurance pricing. Art 6(3)/(4) style documentation is kept (G-40).

title: Risk management system
reasoning: Required of providers of high-risk systems. Not required here. Adopted voluntarily (Art 95 idea) because it is the clearest published method for AI risk management; implemented through G-42 and the risk register.

title: Data and data governance
reasoning: Written for training, validation and test data of high-risk systems. The firm does not train the model. Applied in spirit to evaluation data and to what goes into the context window (G-20, G-21).

title: Technical documentation
reasoning: High-risk provider duty. Adopted as good practice (G-44).

title: Record-keeping
reasoning: High-risk systems must support automatic event logging. Adopted because logging is also the base for security monitoring and incident reconstruction (G-29).

title: Transparency and provision of information to deployers
reasoning: High-risk provider duty towards deployers. Applied in spirit to the information given to approvers and staff (G-17, G-44).

title: Human oversight
reasoning: High-risk duty. Adopted for Tier 3 actions, handoff and the kill switch (G-06, G-09, G-10, G-19, G-32, G-43). Art 14(4)(a)-(e) used as a checklist for what approvers must be able to do.

title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
reasoning: High-risk duty. Used as the security baseline for the agent, including its list of AI-specific attacks in Art 15(5) (poisoning, adversarial inputs, confidentiality attacks).

title: Obligations of providers of high-risk systems
reasoning: Applies if the system becomes high-risk. The firm would then be provider as well as deployer because it builds and puts the system into service under its own name (my reading).

title: Quality management system
reasoning: High-risk provider duty. Parts adopted through change management and independent review (G-36, G-45).

title: Documentation keeping; automatically generated logs
reasoning: Retention targets adopted through G-30 and G-39.

title: Responsibilities along the AI value chain
reasoning: Matters when roles shift between provider, deployer and model supplier. Shapes the contract checks in G-26 and G-25.

title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk systems
reasoning: Not mandatory here. Used as the model for deployer practice: assigned oversight (26(2)), monitoring and suspension (26(5)), log retention (26(6), at least six months, with a rule for financial institutions to satisfy it through their existing rules).

title: Fundamental-rights impact assessment
reasoning: Required for deployers of Annex III 5(b) and 5(c) systems, among others. Not triggered while scope excludes credit scoring and life/health insurance pricing. A voluntary version is part of G-42.

title: Conformity assessment; declaration; registration
reasoning: Apply to high-risk systems. Registration of an Art 6(3) self-assessed non-high-risk system under Annex III would apply only if the firm relied on the derogation for an Annex III use case, which it does not.

title: Disclosure of interaction with AI
reasoning: Systems designed to interact directly with people must tell them they are dealing with AI unless it is obvious. Applies from 2 Aug 2026 (G-15).

title: Marking of synthetic content
reasoning: Text the agent generates is arguably covered, but how it applies to chat replies in a service channel is an open interpretation question. Track the Commission's guidance. A grace period to 2 Dec 2026 exists only for generative systems placed on the market before 2 Aug 2026, so a new system gets none.

title: Emotion recognition and biometric categorisation
reasoning: No emotion recognition or biometric categorisation is used; G-16 forbids emotion inference.

title: Deepfakes and public-interest text
reasoning: The agent does not produce deepfakes or text published to inform the public on matters of public interest.

title: Post-market monitoring by providers
reasoning: Provider duty for high-risk systems. Adopted through G-31 and G-34.

title: Reporting of serious incidents
reasoning: Applies to high-risk systems. The runbook (G-33) names this clock so it is ready if scope changes. Existing clocks that apply today: personal-data breach rules, DORA major-incident rules and NIS2 reporting for the firm.

title: Right to explanation of individual decisions
reasoning: Applies to decisions taken using certain high-risk systems. No such decisions are made. G-19 gives the right to a person anyway.

title: Codes of conduct for voluntary application of specific requirements
reasoning: The basis for choosing to apply high-risk requirements voluntarily.
